Subject: Re: Paragon Health – MSA & Order Form: DPA redlines + SCCs follow-up

Hi all —

I reviewed Paragon's DPA redline v3 (attached). High-level summary and our proposed positions below. See inline comments in attached PDF; pulling out priority items here so Sales/Procurement know our negotiation posture.

1) Subprocessor notice period: Paragon asks for 30 days. We can accept 30 days for planned additions; for emergency/process continuity scenarios we propose a shorter immediate notice with retrospective notification and limitation to specific classes. Proposed language: we will provide at least 30 days' notice for planned additions; in emergency scenarios notice will be provided as soon as practicable.

2) Audit rights / SOC2: We provide annual SOC2 Type II and will provide a regular evidence package on request after an NDA. We cannot allow unrestricted on-site audits for cloud-hosted infrastructure. Proposed clause: evidence package + auditor report, with on-site audits limited to exceptional circumstances and with cost allocation.

3) SCCs & TIA: Our privacy team drafted a transfer-impact addendum template (TIA) and runs a supplier assessment. For Paragon's EU data, we will rely on EU Commission SCCs supplemented by our TIA. We can provide the TIA executive summary and the subprocessors list. For full TIA attachment, we may need a short confidentiality addendum.

4) Data retention & deletion: tighten the mutual-delete certification window to 60 days post-contract termination; propose standard proof-of-deletion for customer-owned storage.

5) Liability caps / carveouts: some of Paragon's proposed unlimited liability language is a hard stop. We propose the standard Redwood liability cap in MSA plus exceptions for gross negligence/willful misconduct.

Attachments: Paragon_MSA_orderform_v2_redline.pdf (redline on commercial), SCCs_TIA_Draft.pdf (privacy team comments).

Next steps: Marissa / Monica, can you prepare an internal consolidated redline (DPA + MSA tie-outs) and a short customer-facing memo answering the SCCs/TIA questions? Elena — after we finalize internal positions we will share a consolidated DPA redline and the TIA executive summary. Target: internal sign-off by EOD tomorrow (Aug 5).

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Privacy & Contracts | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
From: Elena Rossi <elena@paragonhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Briggs <tbriggs@paragonhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Paragon Health – MSA & Order Form: DPA redlines + SCCs follow-up

Thanks Karthik — useful summary. A couple clarifying questions before your consolidated redline: 

- For the SCCs/TIA: can you confirm whether Redwood's TIA will include an attestation that there are no technical controls that would prevent Paragon from meeting its own regulatory obligations (e.g., data subject access, erasure)? We just need enough detail to present to our compliance committee.

- Subprocessors: Paragon's security team requires a 30-day window to review new subprocessors before they are allowed to process our data; are you able to offer a mechanism for expedited review or an allow-list for high-risk categories?

If you can provide a redline + a short FAQ addressing the above, procurement may be able to accept commercial terms quicker.

Best,
Elena

Subject: Re: Paragon Health – MSA & Order Form: DPA redlines + SCCs follow-up

Elena —

Appreciate the prompt review/questions. Quick response and plan: 

1) TIA attestation: We will provide an executive TIA summary that explicitly calls out the controls we rely on for customer obligations (access controls, encryption in transit/at rest, role-based access, incident response). The summary will state whether any of our platform features limit Paragon's ability to comply with DSARs/erasure; in short, there are no technical constraints preventing Paragon from exercising data subject rights. The full TIA will accompany the consolidated DPA redline under a simple confidentiality addendum.

2) Subprocessor review: We cannot commit to an unrestricted 30-day hold-for-approval process for each new subprocessor. Suggested compromise: we will provide a 30-day notice for planned additions and offer Paragon an expedited review queue (priority review within 7 business days) for subprocessors classified as high-risk by Paragon's security team, with a simple form to trigger the expedited review. We will also provide a rolling allow-list option for critical subprocessors (subject to mutual agreement).

3) Deliverables & timeline: Attached is a consolidated redline package (DPA + MSA tie-outs) and a short FAQ addressing SCCs/TIA, subprocessor notice, and SOC2 evidence. We plan to:

- Share consolidated redline (attached) and TIA executive summary: by EOD today.
- If acceptable, we can prepare an orderform update and DocuSign envelope for signatures within 48 hours of commercial sign-off.

Attachments: Paragon_MSA_orderform_v2_redline.pdf; SCCs_TIA_Draft.pdf

Please confirm if the expedited review flow works for Paragon and whether you need an NDA for the SOC2 evidence. If yes, we can share a short mutual NDA and then the evidence bundle.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
